utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated. Before we start, a very short scheduling order. The Chamber has made the following decision: Trial Chamber II of the International Tribunal, noting the temporary unavailability of Judge Fassi Fihri on the morning of Friday, the 27th September, 2002, due to an urgent pressing matter noting that under Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the remaining Judges of the Chamber may order that the hearing of the case continue for a period of not more than three days if satisfied, that it's in the interests of justice to do so, noting the consent of the parties to proceed under Rule 15 bis expressed orally in Court on Wednesday, 25 September, 2002, Livenote page 107, lines 2 to 13, hereby decides to proceed in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri under Rule 15 bis on Friday 27 September from 9.30 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. in Courtroom II. Followed by the signature of the Judge. Then I learned that there is an interest of the parties to have the 65 ter (i) meeting tomorrow. This will be held immediately after the end of the Prosecutor's case. We'll say the meeting will take place 15 minutes later or immediately after the Prosecutor's case in Room M149. In addition, I heard that it's envisaged to try to finalise tomorrow already at 1.00. This would mean that it would facilitate the planning of tomorrow's day, especially for Judge Fassi Fihri, so let us know immediately when you have more concrete information on this. Other urgent matters? No. Then, please, proceed with the cross-examination. Before doing so, after these preliminary remarks, we have to hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, my name is Andrew Cayley. I appear on behalf of the Prosecutor together with case manager Ruth Karper. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Before I return to the attack by this Muslim group on the town of Prijedor where Major Karlica was killed on May 30th, 1992, I would like to clarify one point from your testimony these last two days, if I may. Sir, I realise from your testimony that you confined yourself to the documents only that you selected and then in part identified for us. However, in order to give us an objective analysis, did you review and analyse the materials that were considered by the OTP, namely, the trial attorneys in this case against Dr. Stakic, under Rule 68 known otherwise as exculpatory documentation? Do you understand my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. Ostojic, yes. I believe I did review material that may have been exculpatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me, if I may, show you a letter that was given to us September 24th, immediately before the commencement of your testimony, although it's dated the night before. And it lists 97 specific items that the OTP considers to be under Rule 68 exculpatory. However, before I do, I'd like to know whether you yourself, as you indicated to us yesterday and the day before, did you go out and find this material, or was there actually instances wherein the OTP gave you material to review in connection with the military report that you provided us?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost all the material that I used for the report was a result of my own searches, either on the OTP databases or materials that I was informed about by investigative team. There were some materials in relation to the non-Serb resistance that I wasn't made aware of until the -- a draft of the report had been completed or drafted. Those were, in particular, the Ramic book or diary which I hadn't been aware of. And having been made aware of that, I duly looked at it and read it and, in fact, incorporated some extracts into the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, would the usher be kind enough to show the witness the letter dated September 23rd, 2002, by Ms. Joanna Korner to Mr. Branko Lukic in connection specifically with this topic of Rule 68 exculpatory documentation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would the Defence counsel be kind enough to provide the Judges with another copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will be able to, yes, Your Honour. However, in our attempt to get here in a timely manner, I left it in the Defence counsel room in all seriousness. And I think if the witness would be kind enough just to put it on the ELMO, then we could look at it and I will provide a copy because I'd like also to identify and hopefully get it admitted in as an exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Previously I forgot to mention that the scheduling order I read out bears the Exhibit Number J18. It should be distributed now, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Brown, do you see the letter that I'm referencing regarding Rule 68 dated September 23rd, 2002?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Within that document, there lists approximately 97 items referencing specifically the 1st Krajina Corps, the 43rd Motorised Brigade, the 343rd Motorised Brigade that the OTP trial attorneys suggest fall within Rule 68. Looking through that, and if you don't mind just briefly going through each page just so that the Court and all of us can see it, since I did not provide a complete copy for anyone, and if the technicians can scan away so we can get the complete page on the screen, this, sir, is actually the second page. It starts on the first page below the actual correspondence to Mr. Lukic. Within this document and these 97 items listed by the OTP, can you tell us, sir, how many of those documents you included in your objective report regarding the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the first time I've seen this reference and this letter. And without going through each ERN number and each document individually, I would be unable to do that at this moment. I'm trying to see if any of the documents I recognise just simply by the title, and some I do. But I think in order for me to fully answer your question, I would have to go through each individual document. For example, I notice one there relating to 1st Krajina Corps command authorisation letter, number 741, to engage prisoners of war in the felling of trees. Now again, I would have to be a bit cautious here because I would have to go back to the original document, but I believe that document relates to Manjaca prison camp in Banja Luka Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm suggesting to you, if I may, since I had a little extra time these last few days, that none of the documents that are presented on this Rule 68 appear in your report. Would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only answer that if I went through each individual document and saw the content. As I say, I recognise one or two that I know have no real bearing on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I also notice, sir, that within the documentation provided by the OTP under Rule 68 the report that you say was exhaustive by Jusuf Rahmic is not included in is there, is it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The Rule 68 correspondence and documentation.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to go through each page. I'd have to take your word that it's not on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: For the purposes of -- excuse me, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. President, just so the record is clear, that document has already been disclosed to the Defence. So whether it's on this list or not is immaterial. The Defence had that document, the Jusuf Rahmic document to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't know whether the parties can agree on this procedure. I think it's, for the witness, unfair attempt to put him in a kind of guessing game. This document evidently, as he has said, he has never seen before. So it would be for the Prosecutor to give an explanation why this document, why so late, and what is the basis for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We always will accept the Court's instruction on this. But I think I could answer the questions, and I think that I have a fair inclination as to the basis for it. But if the Court wishes, we'll accept that instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First, we should go to the primary source, and then let's talk about hearsay. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: My understanding, Mr. President, looking at this particular letter, and let's be clear at the start in respect of the Rule 68 obligation. The Court knows it is an extremely wide obligation that the Prosecutor has, and to quote the rule directly, we are obliged to disclose any material which is known to us which in any way tends to suggest the innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or may affect the credibility of Prosecution evidence. In exercising that duty, we interpret that rule very widely. And this material is material that was regarded as Rule 68 in the Brdjanin/Talic case. And we felt that if it was disclosed in that case as potentially Rule 68, we had an obligation to do the same in this case. It doesn't necessarily mean to say in any way that it's relevant to the report of Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for this explanation. Anything to add from your side?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, if I may proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, you are also preparing a report for the Brdjanin/Talic case as you have heard from Mr. Cayley as well as a report in the case of Plavsic and Krajisnik. In connection with that, and when you look at all the parametres suggested by Mr. Cayley that the evidence may be relevant and may point to the innocence of the accused, Dr. Stakic, don't you think, Mr. Brown, that you should have received that letter, should have been notified of that letter, should have been given those documents so that your "objective" report can truly be presented in the fashion that you suggest that it is? Do you understand the question, Mr. Brown?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I can fully answer the question to be truthful. All I can say is that I wasn't given this letter on the day of -- the day before my testimony. All I can say is from a brief observation of the content of the letter, that I recognise some of the documentation contained within it. I would argue from the documentation I do see here, that it is not directly relevant to operations in Prijedor by the Bosnian Serb army. I qualify that by saying that I would have to look at every individual document, and this is the first time I've seen it. I can't comment on why, you know, the document was not passed to me. My report also was written in June and published, I believe, on the 18th of July. But I don't think I'm in a position really to give you more of an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I mean, it seems fair. If I can now turn to the May 30th, 1992, attack on the town of Prijedor that we concluded yesterday. I have a couple more questions on this. On page 27, sir, of your report, again, although my pages are not numbered, I numbered them myself starting with page 1 being the cover sheet, where you identify the document as being "military developments, Prijedor Municipality, from 1991 to 1992." On page 27, as I suggest --

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- discusses an armed group of non-Serbs carried out an abortive attack in the town of Prijedor. Did you, sir, as a military analyst determine (a) the number or how big this armed group was?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you determined on your own that it was how big?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military reports at the time indicate that it was about 80 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Earlier you said that some of the documentation with respect to integrity that Mr. Cayley discussed with you, the documents that you reviewed, some were given to you -- or to the OTP I should say, excuse me, by the Bosnian federation. Did you at any time ask the OTP or the trial attorneys from the OTP - it's a little confusing because you work there, too - did you ever ask them to say, Let's request from the Bosnian federation documents to determine who these individuals were who committed this armed attack on the town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. The report wasn't about indicating which individuals in particular had attacked Prijedor. I take it for granted the attack happened. I take it for granted from the documentation that it occurred on the dates that the Serb documents indicate. And I would assume that the references that they have contained within those documents to be accurate. And what I wanted to do in relation to that was flag up that an attack had happened, that it was about 80 Muslims had attacked the town, that they had killed sentries on the bridge, and attempted to attack personnel in the hotel in Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, that personnel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, wait until the translation is ready.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And so, that was what was put in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you as a military analyst, sir, determine how many snipers the Muslim or the non-Serb, as you call them, armed group had at the town of Prijedor while these 80 men were coming to attack the town?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reports from the Serb documentation said there was an attack of about 80 men and that there was a secondary attack of about 8 men from the area of Donja Puharska. I took those figures at face value and the reported events contained within the military reports at face value, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, militarily speaking, when the report suggests that there was an armed group, can you tell me what that would mean? Armed in what capacity? And I would like you to keep that in conjunction with the very next paragraph that says there was "heavy fighting." If you put those two together, sir, militarily speaking, what does that signify to you?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there was a serious conflict at that period as a result of this attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, as a military analyst, determine whether this group who attacked the town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992, consisted of Green Berets, the Patriotic League, and/or other Muslim-based paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, not in that detail. Going by the reports, the reports themselves, call them Green Berets. I don't believe the word or the phrase "Patriotic League" is used. Muslim extremists are used. And clearly, this was an armed group of non-Serbs who attacked the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you determine whether this group, sir, by any of the reports including Mr. Jusuf Rahmic's report, whether or not this group of armed non-Serbs consisted of one or more than one ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to go over the Rahmic book again. It's not the easiest piece of work to read, and he does make some references to it. I'd have to review that to give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there any indication from the documentation that you reviewed, sir, that the group that attacked the town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992, was something other than a Muslim ethnically-based group considered here to be a paramilitary formation, part of the Patriotic League, or part of the Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb documentation, as I've said, indicates that it was an armed group of Muslim ethnicity. I haven't seen any reference to the Patriotic League. And there are general references throughout the Serb documentation when they refer to "armed groups" as "Green Berets."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Help me with this, Mr. Brown: When a town is attacked by an outside force, armed group, as you've identified, regardless of whether it's 80 or approximately 80 men, which includes heavy fighting where they neutralise the actual bridge over the Sana, and they have sniper capacity, have killed a major such as Major Karlica, tell me what the military response, sir, should be by the nonattackers?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say what the response should be as a generality. What I can say is what the response was. The response was to, in essence, counterattack and very quickly take control of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Militarily speaking, sir, isn't it a fact that when a military group such as the Republika Srpska or as you call it the VRS, if they get attacked, they are required to do what? Return hostile fire, drop their arms, or are they, sir, required to actually required to return hostile fire, secure the area, proceed to capture the perpetrators of the attack? Which, if any?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearly, if a military is attacked, they would have under their rules of engagement the right to defend themselves and potentially carry out these acts that you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm a little hesitant --

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in fact, that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm a little hesitant to talk about rules of engagement today. But let's turn to the attack on Kozarac on May 24th, 1992. Are you familiar, sir, with any evidence that the OTP presented and that was produced for this Trial Chamber that when a military convoy proceeded from the Banja Luka/Prijedor Road going west towards Prijedor, that it was attacked by a Muslim barricade and/or checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've highlighted that in the report, that there was an incident in Kozarac, I believe, on the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At which fire was opened from a barricade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Again, if I'm not mistaken, help me with this: Did the Serb military attack the barricade or did the people who were at this barricade, at this checkpoint, open fire initially on the Serb convoy that was passing through? What's your objective analysis of those -- that situation?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following on from the attack on Hambarine, there was an incident at the barricade in Kozarac at which fire was opened by those manning the barricades. The result was a large-scale attack on the wider area of Kozarac. That was a sequence of events that I saw from the documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Take it one step at a time. The convoy, sir, that passed through the Banja Luka/Prijedor Road was nowhere near the village of Hambarine, was it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was sent from where, sir? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was sent from Prijedor, and they were going to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, it was from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And Banja Luka is to the east of Prijedor. Right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And they would take the road called Banja Luka/Prijedor Road. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact, sir, did you see any evidence in your objective analysis to determine whether or not the military made a proclamation or an announcement which requested that the Muslim checkpoints on the road of Banja Luka/Prijedor, that they moved back 100 metres so that the convoy can pass without any hinderance and without any potential confrontation. Did you hear or review any of those witness statements or documentation?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen not from the documentation that detail that you've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From who? Because I thought your report was based solely on the documentation in this case and solely on, ultimately, the 150 documents that you utilised to come up with this objective report.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the documentation I have not seen that announcement to move 100 metres so that the convoy could pass without any hinderance and without any potential confrontation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, sir: Point to me where in your objective report --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, slow down, and don't overlap. It takes time, especially with the French translation, as we all know, and make sure that it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, if I may, Your Honour, if the mic... Here it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's good now with the French booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, as I was starting to say, point to me where in your objective report it indicates that you even considered the fact that this military convoy going from Banja Luka to Prijedor sought or wanted to have clear access and requested that the Muslims who manned -- armed and manned the checkpoint on the road at Jakupovici to move back 100 metres?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Asked and answered twice, Your Honour, by the witness. He stated he hasn't seen any documentation in his review that indicates this fact that Mr. Ostojic is alluding to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may be heard. I don't want to in any way try to interpret Mr. Brown's testimony at this time. However, it seemed to me that first he said he had heard it, and then when I asked him from whom, he said it was in the documentation. And then I'm following up and saying just point to the report where it is that you consider it. Those are the three elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Categorically, he did not say that he had seen any such matter in the documents, and I think Your Honours, he has been asked this question twice. He has answered it twice. If you wish he can be asked it a third time and I presume the answer will be exactly the same. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, do you think that that's a significant fact, if true, that there was an announcement by the military that the Muslims who were armed and manning the checkpoint move back 100 metres in your considerations for your report?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is to repeat what I've already said: I have not seen in the documentation that I have reviewed either in the daily combat reports or other material that the Muslims were ordered back 100 metres --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think I said requested, but whatever.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Requested. And all I can say is from the chronology of events that occurred what the documents tell us. But as I said, I have not seen a reference in relation to that --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just for the record, the OTP is from now on represented also by Mr. Koumjian. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, again you mentioned during our discussions with respect to the attack on the town of Prijedor and the significance of what the military response should be, you used the word that militarily has some significance, namely, "rules of engagement." With respect to the attack on Kozarac, sir, when a military convoy is attacked and when clearly it has been established that in the first vehicle, one of the military personnel were shot and killed by the armed men at the barricade, what is the response of the military supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me as a professional soldier and what I think from that respect or from what the documents tell me?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me try it this way. Your analysis in your report is based upon your education, your experience, as well as your review and digestion, if you will, of the material before you. Based on those three factors, sir, I don't see how -- although you may be able to separate it, tell me whether or not the military was justified in returning fire, whether they were justified in securing the area, whether they were justified, sir, in capturing the men who perpetrated the attack who killed the initial military personnel in the convoy, and whether they were justified, sir, in responding to this hostile fire? If you can distinguish from whether that answer would differ from your education, from your experience, and/or from the documentation, please share that with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: These were ten questions in one. And I think it would also facilitate your work, Mr. Ostojic, if you could once again go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Sorry, excuse me, Mr. Ostojic. I think it's also fair to point out, I mean Mr. Ostojic has given his interpretation of the evidence in this case. And my understanding is that we haven't heard evidence from anybody that was at that checkpoint. And the evidence that has been heard, and that's a matter for you to judge whether it's reliable, indicates that in fact it was the Serbs who attacked the checkpoint. So I think in prefacing the question to the witness, Mr. Ostojic should actually represent the evidence that has been heard in this trial and not his interpretation of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't want to get into a debate about that, but there was specifically one witness who said he raised two guns and wanted to have an indication that there was more rapid fire and more men there. But that's not the point. If I'm wrong on it, then on redirect Mr. Cayley can give a hypothetical question and he can give his facts based on the OTP's interpretation of what occurred. Ultimately, the Court will be the trier of those facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this is a concrete point. It's for us to evaluate at the end of the day all testimony. And please understand that I will never indicate what we now see as the result of the evidence provided for us. But please continue with small, interpretable, and understandable questions and facilitate the work of our witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, when a military convoy is attacked by hostile, armed men on a convoy, are they justified, sir, to return fire?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they most likely are.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are they justified, sir, to capture the perpetrators of the attack?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe they would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are they justified, sir, in securing the area for purposes of safety for themselves?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the immediacy of the site they were shot from or are you talking a wider area? Can you be a bit more specific there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To break it down, first the immediacy, and then the wider area.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really comment I suppose on the wider area, and that would depend on the individual case you were discussing. But it would seem likely that the military would want to secure the immediacy of the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not just likely, Mr. Brown, it's a protocol that's required and it's a protocol that every military personnel in every country when under hostile attack actually follows. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it probably is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it also justified, sir, for the military to secure the area for the safety of the population at large, since there was a hostile attack, for the civilians?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not really sure I can comment on that, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it justified, sir, for the military to secure not only the area where the hostile activities occurred, but also for the protection and the safety of the civilians to go into this wider area and to secure it, to protect the civilians, to move them out of the area?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can comment on this hypothetical because each case would have to be, you know, looked on its own merits. And when you are moving into issues of moving out populations for the protection of civilians, I think you've gone way beyond this particular incident of fire being opened from a checkpoint on a convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, obtain any information from the sources that you identified who were - I forget the term you used - legitimate. Did you ask the OTP trial attorneys to obtain from the Bosnian federation any decrees or any documentation which would indicate to you why the convoy was attacked by the Muslim checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. However, I would like to indicate that in some of the material, the handwritten notes, and the Rahmic diary or work, that there are references to individual acts of provocation which people are concerned with for the reasons that this would escalate, escalate issues in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From those -- from those references, I did not get the impression that a number of people were happy about, i.e., non-Serbs were happy about potential acts of provocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A couple more issues on this point and I would like to move on in light of the time constraints. Do you consider the attack on the convoy as a "provocation"?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the perspective of the Serbs, it might well have been viewed as an act of provocation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's take the perspective of the Brits, sir, how would you view it as an objective military analyst when a military convoy is attacked by armed Muslims at a checkpoint. Would you consider that to be a provocation or not?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potentially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this: In reviewing the documentation at large that you did, including the Dr. Stakic case as well as the two other matters that we mentioned, Brdjanin/Talic, Plavsic and Krajisnik, did you ever, sir, in your attempt to create this objective report come up with any documentation which would suggest that there was some order or decree from the Muslim leadership in Sarajevo which instructed certain Muslim insurgent groups to attack military convoys? Have you ever come around or seen that type of information?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me turn, if I may, to the Hambarine attack which happened May 22nd, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, in that report make a conclusion as to whether or not the attack and the killing of the two VRS soldiers, as you've identified them, and the wounding of the remaining four, did you consider that to be a "provocation"?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make any particular judgement on that. The attack took place on the 22nd. The documentation that I reviewed did not go into every single issue and did not give the full details of the events surrounding that individual event.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This was also at a checkpoint, correct, at Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is reported as being at a checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is there any doubt in your mind that it was a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, no. From the documentation, it makes it evident there was a checkpoint there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is there any doubt, sir, from the documentation that you reviewed that, in fact, the hostilities were initiated by the armed Muslims who were at the checkpoint against the soldiers who were trying to pass through?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the soldier was doing at the checkpoint. The documents don't give any indication of what they were there to do, whether they were there as part of the potential disarmament operation that had been apparently planned for that day. But it's clear that the soldiers were shot, a number killed, and a number wounded, and fire was opened from the area of the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, based upon your education, experience, and analysis of the documents reach a conclusion as to whether this was a provocation by the Muslims at the checkpoint against the Serbs? Sorry. I'm apologising to the interpreters, Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents don't in themselves indicate, as I said, the exact sequence of events and what happened there. So I can't explain from the documentation the sequence of events. To give a judgement on whether it was a deliberate act of provocation or whether some incident had happened that the Muslims at the checkpoint may have felt threatened, I can't -- I can't give you an explanation from that -- from that -- from the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If it's not a provocation, what would you consider it, militarily speaking, sir? Just a simple confrontation?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only reiterate, I can't -- it could well have been a confrontation. It could well have been an incident that was initiated on one or either side. It could well have been an act of provocation by the residents of Hambarine. However, from the documentation, I can't make a judgement on that. All I know from the documentation is that the incident occurred, that a number of Serb soldiers were killed, and a number were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would it be presumptuous on my part, since you don't have the information which would necessarily lead you to conclude whether it was a provocation or a confrontation or just an incident, you cannot determine, militarily speaking, whether or not there was justification for a response to that hostile attack, and similarly you wouldn't be able to -- I'll stop there. Again, a long question. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I can make a judgement on whether -- or the type of response that should have resulted from that. My report simply indicates a sequence of events that occurred in Hambarine, as I've indicated. The attack was significant after the incident. And within a day, they were reporting -- the corps were reporting that the area was under the control of the military --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's what the documents tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you please turn to your Power Point presentation with the caption "Military Preparations Relating to Prijedor." And we're moving on to another topic, I think.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like me to put it on the ELMO, or can I read it from the hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would be grateful if you could put it on the ELMO for our dear interpreters. Mr. Brown, may we proceed.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Those are the five items that you list as being a summary within your report which indicate that the military was making preparations in relation to Prijedor, in essence, constituting a war. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said they were mobilising for war, I believed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mobilising for war. But those are the five items in summary. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, in looking at this as an objective military analyst, as you are, sir, let's take the fourth item which is the enhanced state of readiness. Okay? With respect to that item, sir, in order to be objective, shouldn't the Court know that on April 4th, 1992, the presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina took over the authority from the presidency -- people's assembly and proclaimed "state of imminent threat of war" which was, sir, in essence, 10 to 12 days prior to when the Serb Republic, as you claim, made preparations for this, as you identify, "enhanced state of readiness".

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't want to interrupt until I was sure, but this isn't a question. It's a statement of fact. Where's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll stipulate that it's a statement of fact. But let me then restate the question, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so. Short question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Short. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, did you consider for purposes of your objective analysis as to why the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina declared, as you claim, on April 12th this "enhanced state of readiness"? I think the 16th of April. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you consider, sir, the fact that on April 4th, 1992, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, having taken over the authority of the people's assembly in Bosnia and Herzegovina proclaimed 8 to 12 days earlier a "state of imminent threat of war"?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where in your report does it say, sir, that the Serbs - as you identify them throughout your report, the Bosnian Serbs - where does the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- where does it suggest that that government -- in response to this "state of immediate threat of war" issued by Alija Izetbegovic, where does it put it in perspective? An objective analyst like you would have shared that information. Wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said at the beginning, this was not an exhaustive report on every issue relating to 1992 in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During my analysis, I looked at the sequence of events in relation to the Bosnian Serb military; and in particular, in relation to Prijedor. When I looked at some of the documents in relation to weapon deadlines, the 16th of April decision on the mobilisation of the Serb TO seemed to be a start point in relation to the sequence of events that ended up occurring in Prijedor Municipality. I also looked at trying to understand why that date was important. And you're right that in a number of days prior to that decision, that the Bosnian government did issue that decree and, I believe, some days later actually issued a mobilisation instruction. I looked at those documents and assessed that the decisions taken by the Bosnian government were in response to activities in Bijeljina and other areas in Bosnia, not Prijedor. Secondarily, when I looked at the documents, the handwritten notes, the Rahmic diary, the Serb documents themselves, it struck me that the non-Serbs' mobilisation or preparations were not as developed. And I believe I covered that in the report in relation to Prijedor Municipality. Those are the reasons that I didn't include the Bosnian government's decisions. But the main one being, as I've highlighted on a number of occasions, this report and the tasking I was given was in relation to the Bosnian Serb military in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. So if I were to suggest to you, sir, that your report is not objective because it did not include the fact that 12 days earlier, there was an order stating that there was a state of immediate threat of war and that that certainly impacted or was somehow relevant or as you claim linked to items that were happening throughout that region works I be wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Asked and answered, and rhetorical question. And argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, in your response, you wanted to move away from the issue of enhanced state of readiness. In your report, however, you list that as a separate item from mobilisation. I recognise that on April 6th, as do you, sir, that there was by the Bosnian Muslim government a declaration that they were no longer part of the Former Yugoslavia and actually seceded. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As an objective military analyst, is that significant when placing things in proper context as to what the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was doing? To at least identify that date as a timetable?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only return to the remit that I was giving in the report and the limitations of it. It relates to Prijedor Municipality. It's not a report charting the political developments of -- all aspects of political developments in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The reason that I placed the 16th of April documents in there was because I believed it had an impact on events in Prijedor that could be charted through other documentation. I have not included lots of other documentation that may have had an impact in terms of Serb material from 1991 or 1990. So...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I want to stick to the 1992 period at the very least in the limited time. And you're right, we should move away from the politics because your remit was not to look at the political situation but only the military. Speaking of military issues, though, are you familiar, sir, that on April 8th, 1992, before any of the items that you list under the caption military preparations relating to Prijedor that, in fact, the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina enacted a decree abolishing the republican Territorial Defence staff that existed and issued an order to create a new Territorial Defence staff of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina by order and decree, since I think you already know this, 01-011-302/92?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that decree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you also, sir -- and it's not in your report. Right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not in the report, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It happened before any of the five items that you list on this Power Point presentation in the caption "military preparations relating to Prijedor." Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened prior to the 16th of April, mobilisation of the Serb TO, certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, also, are you familiar with the decree with the number 01-011-306/92 when there was a decree from the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, which unified all armed forces in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, April 9th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at that document again. I cannot remember the content of the document and the various reference numbers. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking you recall such a thing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did it happen generally speaking if you can remember before or after the five items that you put on your Power Point presentation "military preparations relating to Prijedor"?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened to be prior to the 15th -- or 15th and 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this so I can understand: In keeping it in proper perspective or in proper context, wouldn't that be at the very least relevant in your report? To say that instead of suggesting that the Serbs were creating these movement of units, that the Serbs were creating this mobilisation, that they were enhancing the state of readiness, wouldn't it have been an objective and fair way to state that it was a response to something that was happening within the republic, within the region, less than ten days prior to their pronouncements and decisions?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only return to the answer given you in the past. This was a report relating to the Bosnian Serb military activity in Prijedor Municipality. It may well have been that the 15th of April and 16th of April decisions were done in response to the Bosnian government. But you could go back to why did the Bosnian government feel that it had a need to mobilise? And one of the justifications that they were giving at the time was because of the actions that occurred in Bijeljina. Do you then take what had happened in Bijeljina and go back prior to late March 1992 to another start point? All I can say is that this report was about Bosnian Serb military actions in Prijedor. And in relation to the mobilisation of the non-Serbs, from the documents that I have seen, I do not see a large-scale mobilisation. I see the mobilisation list which appears to have been from May 1992, early May 1992, which is a list of names and signatures with a small number of weapons, in comparison to the total numbers on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. So a reasonable person who wants to give this Chamber an objective military analytical report would have at the very least, wouldn't you agree, Mr. Brown, contact through the Office of the Prosecutor the Bosnian federation individuals and ask them: "Give us the complete list of all the Territorial Defence units that you had in existence in the territory on or around the Prijedor Municipality in 1992." Wouldn't you think so?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have those lists, Mr. Ostojic, I'd be happy to make comments on them. I have not seen lists of that sort of material, apart from the ones that I've referenced in my report. I have looked on the databases for them and I have not seen them. If you have that sort of material that you believe might change my assessment or influence it, then I'd be happy to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that. But I'm asking you whether or not you contacted the Bosnian federation authorities and requested that of them, to give you a complete breakdown of what the Territorial Defence membership was in the Prijedor area in 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not contact the Bosnian federation authorities, and I worked off the material that I obtained during my searching.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: If, as a person who is asked to give a report, and if something is missing, do you follow up? Do you make any inquiries in order to get a complete picture and a proper perspective? Do you ask anyone to fill any gaps with respect to the objectivity of your report or analysis? Or do you simply proceed with weaving the documents that are given to you and coming up with a report such as you did?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the witness gave us four or five times the basis for his report, and thereby the question is answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to the first item on this Power Point presentation "Weapons Deadlines" sir, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From your analysis, sir, did you determine whether the request to turn in weapons was made exclusively and solely to the Muslim population in the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The requests, Your Honours, talk of illegally-held weapons and disarming paramilitary groups. They do not on their own indicate which ethnic group was to be disarmed. But I see no documentary evidence of any Serb or any operation to disarm weapons that may have been held by Serbs. And the operations that took place against predominantly non-Serbs villages in Prijedor were often couched in the phrase "operations to disarm paramilitary groups or seize illegally held weapons." I have seen no documentary evidence that I've looked at that those types of operations were conducted on Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to operations, if we can, in a few minutes. My question I thought was precise; probably not, though. Let me try to articulate it in a better fashion so that you and I can both understand it, Mr. Brown. The documentation relating specifically to the first point in your Power Point presentation on the military preparations relating to Prijedor the supporting material for that, sir, does not indicate that the authorities requesting that there be a turn over of weapons, illegal or not, by any specific ethnic group; in fact, it was a general request made by the authorities. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question was concrete. The answer was concrete. It may not satisfy the Defence, but answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May we turn, sir, to Document Number S342.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wonder if you could give me either the footnote reference or the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Footnote 49.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you with me, Mr. Brown?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this document, sir, you reviewed it, analysed, but for foundational purposes if I may ask you who prepared the document and to whom was it sent?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was a Prijedor SJB report sent to the Banja Luka security services.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In that report, sir, it identifies that certain conclusions were made regarding the municipality control. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell this Court, sir, in your opinion whether or not Dr. Milomir Stakic sat on the Executive Board of the Municipality of Prijedor on or about 1992 at any time.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unaware whether Dr. Stakic sat on the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, what Dr. Stakic's position was in 1991 or 1992 in the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic was head of the Crisis Staff in Prijedor later, in May 1992. If you can hold on a second whilst I consult my report. Dr. Stakic was also head of the National Defence Council in Prijedor Municipality. I believe he was head of the municipality, but not the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, so that we can be precise, as your report is, in my opinion, can you tell me when you say "head," sir, wasn't there a specific function and title for Dr. Stakic during all those times and in fact, sir, he was never a member of the Executive Board of the Serbian Assembly of Prijedor? Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that was to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact, the government of the Prijedor Municipality was run by, controlled by and from the Executive Board, and not the general opstina skupstine as we have identified it here from time to time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unaware of the workings of various levels of government in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's because your remit was not to go into that political structure. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Since your report seems to span from 1991 to 1992, you're familiar with the late Mr. Cehajic, are you not? As to who he was and what function he played in the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the details. My report spans 1991 only because certain units in Prijedor were in Croatia, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that had an impact in relation to their deployment, their combat readiness, and their exposure. Mr. Cehajic, I know, was a political figure in Prijedor Municipality, and it was not within the remit of my report to conduct any analysis in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, though, because you use the word influence, and I apologise if I'm speaking fast in connection with some of the civilian authorities. In April, specifically the dates we were talking about, April 4th, when this decree from Alija Izetbegovic regarding the immediate threat of war; April 6th, when there was the secession from the Bosnian federation, and maybe I should write this down; April 8th, the decree we read in connection with the Territorial Defence; April 9th, the unification of the army forces. Tell me, sir, if you can, and I accept the fact that the late Mr. Cehajic was a political figure in the municipality of Prijedor in April of 1992. Tell me in your opinion as an analyst what influence, if any, he would have relating to any one of those decrees, declarations, and orders issued by the federal or republic governments?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only answer what I've asked -- answered already. It was not within the remit of my report to look at the political structures and their functioning within Prijedor Municipality. The references that I have used relate to military actions or military issues. So that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think that's all we have, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any questions longer than five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have about 15 minutes, Your Honour, of questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we should have the break now. But before going into the break, please recall that already yesterday and today, and before, I asked for some supporting material on the VP number 8316. This should be ready after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: With your permission, Your Honour, what I intended to do was to do the re-examination and then I have the package of material that you asked for which I was going to put in at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The trial stands adjourned until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Ostojic, we did agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's good to know for the Judges that the parties agree, so please start.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd like to get my version of the -- Your Honour, earlier when we were cross-examining Mr. Brown, we identified a document that we did not have sufficient copies for the Court. With your permission, if the usher would be kind enough to tender it to the Court and the parties, and we would move that this document be admitted into evidence under the next D number, which I think is D29 if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You're extremely correct. D29. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, D29. And at the same time, I have to correct myself on today's transcript as it reads related to our scheduling order, J18. Correct would be J17. Sorry for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, I don't have many questions for you. You were asked earlier today about military activity in the villages of Hambarine and Kozarac in May of 1992. Do you recall that series of questions?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that that, those matters, the attack on Hambarine and Kozarac, were addressed in your report from pages 22 to 27?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you have already made it very clear both on examination-in-chief and cross-examination that this report is exclusively documentary based. And the question I have for you is in respect of your analysis of events in Hambarine and Kozarac. What is the source for all of those documents that you relied upon for the attack in Hambarine and Kozarac, in the majority?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Significant number of military documents, Your Honour, and a number of police-related documents as well. But Serb police and military material.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that they are all Serb police and military material? Is there any other material that you used in making your report on these -- on military activities in these two villages?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in relation to the section you've quoted, I think there are all police and military documents. There are a number of open-source documents I believe that may reflect some activity of the units in those areas. But I believe within the section that you've quoted, I think they are all police and military documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Serb police and military documents?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can move on. Yesterday, you were asked a series of questions relating to the authority of local political figures over the police and the military. Do you recall that series of questioning?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And just for the purposes of the record and to assist Mr. Ostojic, these matters are referred to on page 87, 88, 90, 91. And in particular, I think you'll recall it was put to you that there was absolutely no command responsibility as it relates to Dr. Stakic in either the military and/or the police right. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I want to show you a series of documents which are exhibits in this case very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 71, please. Madam Registrar, if we could have ready 72 and 114, and then we could move quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's a brief document, Mr. Brown. I've tried to select documents for your examination that are brief. Can you read that document through.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like me to put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, could you put it on the ELMO. I don't think there's any particular need to read it through. I would imagine that these documents are already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: They have been read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So there's no necessity. Looking at that document, in your opinion, what does it appear to be?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be a document that references the work of the Crisis Staff, and in particular Article 7, and in relation to that article, it instructs the chief of police and Slobodan Kuruzovic to coordinate security at Prijedor hospital and to report on that if the -- the following morning, or sorry, the following meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And paragraph 2 refers to that instruction as an order, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And who apparently is this document signed by?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic, president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now please look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 72, if you can read it through and let me know when you've read it through. You don't need to read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you give your opinion as an analyst on what this document purports to be.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It also quotes the organisation and work of the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff order which we've discussed over the last few days. And it's an order to the police to check a particular neighbourhood in order to prevent people moving in without authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Who is it apparently signed by?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's president of the Crisis Staff, Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can we now, please, look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 114. Again, sir, if you could just quickly read this document through - again, don't read it out loud - and then let me know when you've read it.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a brief overview, it appears to be a document from the Prijedor police to the Crisis Staff informing the Crisis Staff that various conclusions are being implemented or observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Conclusions from whom?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Taking those three documents together that we've just looked at, the two orders, this document referencing that conclusions are being observed by the police, what is your opinion on the command relationship between the police and the Crisis Staff in Prijedor based on these three documents?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the Crisis Staff were issuing instructions and orders to the police and that Prijedor police were implementing these instructions and referring back to those two instruction that they had observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When you say "observed," that they had received from the Crisis Staff in Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would appear so from these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 79, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I could remind the speakers to pause between questions and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, can you read this document through, and again tell me when you've read it.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what this document purports to be.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a Crisis Staff document, again, referring to articles on the decision and organisation on the work of the Crisis Staff in Prijedor. And it's an order to the Prijedor police and Prijedor regional command ordering them to form a joint intervention platoon and other instructions relating to that, and that they were to report on the activities of this intervention platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do you have your slide show on, or is it switched off?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I switched it off and deleted it from the computer unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You've caught me out there, Mr. Brown. Can you put page 4 of the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the slide on the SDS takeover?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, sorry. It's the one just before that, on the VRS command structure. Now, the document that you have just been referring to, 79, refers to Prijedor regional command. Can you point out Prijedor regional command for us.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So the intermediate command between the 1st Krajina Corps and 43rd Motorised Brigade, 5th Kozara Brigade, and the TO units later, the light infantry brigades within Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let's go back to the document momentarily. Now, this document states "order." Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Who is it signed by apparently?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the Crisis Staff, Dr. Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown, please, Prosecutor's Exhibit 111. Now, Mr. Brown, this is a document that you had previously referred to, but I just want to show it to you to have you look at it and explain. Again, what does this appear to be?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a reference in the Official Gazette of a decision of the 29th of May, Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff stating that Slobodan Kuruzovic, commander of the Territorial Defence, was relieved of his duties and placed under the command of the region. And that it was to be implemented forthwith.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if you look on the original, though, it's not actually signed, the signature block is that of whom?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Milomir Stakic, president, Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And then, sir, the last document that I'd like you to look at, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 116, again, this is a lengthy document. It's the only one unfortunately that was quite lengthy. But if you could just look it over, and it's actually the titles that interest me in particular, a summary of conclusions, orders, and decisions adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question. I think the document doesn't have quite as Mr. Cayley suggests, although I'm sure it was an inadvertent mistake on his part to include the word a summary of conclusions and orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: My apologies. Mr. Ostojic is quite right. Actually, it does say that further down. If you go to the next -- the bottom of the first page, it says a summary of conclusions, orders, and decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the witness is waiting for your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Sorry. Did you have an opportunity to look at the document, Mr. Brown?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you very briefly in your normal, objective, conservative style, briefly explain what this document is?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear to be what it says on face value, which is a summary of decisions relating to police and military issues adopted by the executive committee; and at the bottom, conclusions, orders, and decisions adopted by the Crisis Staff in relation to the SJB and regional command between the periods annotated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In summary, reviewing this document and the last two documents that I've referred to, the Kuruzovic document, and the Formation of the Intervention Platoon document, what conclusions can you draw from those three documents?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the Prijedor command was in a position to be able to issue orders, decisions, and conclusions that affected the work of the regional command and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You just said that the Prijedor command was in a position to --

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The Prijedor Crisis Staff. And from this particular document, the Prijedor municipal executive committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were in a position to do what? I'm sorry, just for the purposes of the record to get this straight.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Were able to or in a position to issue conclusions, orders, and decisions in relation to the regional command and the SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What about the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are references, the document you've just shown us in relation to Kuruzovic, that they could do that with the Territorial Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have got no further questions for the witness. But I know there are a series of documents that you wish to be put into the dossier. I would actually ask, if I may, and if there are no objections from the Defence to put a hard copy of the slide show into evidence, unless that has been done already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the slide show forms part of the report, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It does not, Your Honour. But we have no objection to the Power Point presentation being admitted into evidence. However, if I may, with the Court's permission, if I can just ask a couple questions of the witness based upon the redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe you can wait until you have also, if any, Judges' questions included.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the hard copies of this slide show should follow the report as such, adding just -1. That would be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the point Mr. Ostojic has just raised, recross-examination is something which in principle I object to. Re-examination is a process which basically is a product of the questions that Mr. Ostojic has asked. And in my respectful submission to the Court, that is the end of it, apart from Judges' questions. Mr. Ostojic cannot now go back and start pecking away at matters that I have put to the witness. Mr. Ostojic knew very well that the documents I put to the witness were in the dossier. He could have put as a foundation for his questions to the witness those documents which were in his possession which actually demonstrate completely opposite of what he was putting to the witness. And I don't think it's right that he should be able to ask further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would the Court like to hear our argument on what Mr. Cayley --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, no, no. Step by step. I'm still waiting for some documents, especially the one related to this number 8316, I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have those, Your Honour. The first -- now, again, I have the shorter list which includes that. The first document was a document that you referred to. It was the daily notes of the operative officer within the 5th JNA corps to which the witness made reference regarding a note of the takeover of Prijedor Municipality on the 30th of April of 1992. That was a document that you said that you would wish to refer to. So if I can offer that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That is 1036.033, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S362.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The next matter, Your Honour, is that you had asked me in respect of Exhibit S141, which are the minutes of the 16th assembly meeting. You had stated that that document was only partially admitted into evidence, and you had asked me to identify the pages to which the witness had referred to. And I can do that. They are pages 13, 14, and 15, and 59 and 60 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First question. Objections? This is from the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I understand Mr. Cayley correct, Your Honour, is he just introducing those certain portions for a second time, because I think the practice, if I may, was to have a completeness so that the entirety of it. But for highlighting purposes in his report, I have no objection to those documents being marked and included within Mr. Brown's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When we can read the valued report of the registry, then you could find that under S141 we had only four portions until now. So this would be a third portion of S141, 3A and B respectively. Do we agree on this? Once again, I learned that I was already one number ahead. The last document, indeed, this volume was 361, not S362. Once again, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
